newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 496.50/467.50/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 496.50/467.50/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly weaker at 496.50/497.50 per dollar Wednesday in heavy corporate demand for foreign currency fueled by expectations of further depreciation, traders said.
"Demand is growing every day, especially as corporate clients see the dollar is rising," one trader said.
Traders added that many clients were short on dollars at the end of trading Wednesday and that pressure on the local currency would continue Thursday.
The bolivar has depreciated by 4.50 bolivars per dollar (0.9 percent) over the last week.
Traders said the bolivar's slide had made currency market's increasingly nervous and that expectations of a continued depreciation were high.
Central Bank officials have said that despite the recent slide of the bolivar the exchange rate was well within the limits of the exchange bands system it established a year ago.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
